title: The Industrial Revolution
examples: What was the biggest change during the Industrial Revolution?
How did steam power change daily life?
What were the living conditions like in early factories?

explain.say: The first big change was the steam engine. People used steam to power machines.
Next, machines moved into factories. Factories grouped many machines together.
These new industries caused people to move to cities. This growth is called urbanization.
Working life changed a lot. People often worked long hours for low wages.
In everyday life, think about a modern supermarket. It needs many workers in one place. That is like a factory.
A common mistake is thinking all work moved to factories right away. The change took many decades to happen.

faq.q: Why did the Industrial Revolution start in Britain?
faq.a: Britain had many natural resources like coal and iron. This allowed them to build steam engines and machines easily.
asks: What were the key reasons for Britain's lead?
Why was Britain so good at this change?

faq.q: What was the main source of power before steam engines?
faq.a: Before steam, many places used muscle power from people or animals. Water wheels were also used in some places.
asks: Did they use wind power too?

faq.q: Were all workers treated the same in the new cities?
faq.a: No, the poor often lived in crowded, unsanitary housing. Only the wealthy could afford better living areas.
asks: How did the poor live in the cities?

faq.q: Did factories only make one type of thing?
faq.a: Factories could make many things, but they focused on making items quickly and in huge amounts. This was mass production.

faq.q: How did the steam engine improve travel?
faq.a: Steam power was used on trains and boats. This meant people and goods could travel much faster than before.

facts: The steam engine greatly improved power sources.
Factories allowed for the mass production of goods.
Rapid growth led to overcrowding in cities.
Working hours were often very long for factory workers.

quiz.why: Steam power provided a reliable and strong source of energy for machines.

wrong.0: Wind power was unpredictable and often too weak.
wrong.2: Muscle power was tiring for people and animals to use constantly.
wrong.3: Water wheels only worked when the river level was right.

quiz.say: Grouping many machines together in one building is called what?
quiz.why: A factory was designed to house many machines for efficient, large-scale work.

wrong.0: A market is where goods are sold, not where they are made.
wrong.2: A workshop was usually much smaller and held fewer machines.
wrong.3: A farm is for growing food, not making goods.

quiz.say: If a city suddenly grows very fast due to jobs, what is this process called?
quiz.why: Urbanization specifically describes the rapid growth and change of cities.

wrong.0: Settlement is a general term, but urbanization describes the speed of growth.
wrong.2: Decline means the area is shrinking or getting worse.
wrong.3: Migration is the movement of people, not the resulting growth of the city.
